new_species.name: D-ribulose_C5H10O5

notes.r2190_product_species: Added by R2190-RIBULOSE-20261019 as the product of R2190 only. No producer, consumer or transporter of free D-ribulose is evidenced for Y. lipolytica in this model, so it is a dead end.

new_species.annotation_limits: CHEBI:17173 and MNXM1371690 are Rhea 17389's D-ribulose; MNXR197981 on R2190 uses the alpha-anomer MNXM1371691. Both map to KEGG C00309.

evidence.claim: R07134: C01904 + C00003 <=> C00309 (D-Ribulose) + C00004 + C00080; EC 1.1.1.250; R2190's own kegg.reaction annotation.
D-arabinitol + NAD(+) = D-ribulose + NADH + H(+); EC 1.1.1.250.
D-arabinitol + NAD(+) <=> alpha-D-ribulose + H(+) + NADH; R2190's own metanetx.reaction annotation.
Systematic name D-arabinitol:NAD+ 2-oxidoreductase (D-ribulose-forming), the R2190 name without its suffix.

Wang et al. 2020 (doi:10.1186/s13068-020-01815-8): purified YlAraDH1 (YALI0F02211g = YALI1F03452g) is NAD(H)-dependent, oxidizes D-arabitol, mannitol, D-sorbitol and xylitol, and reduces only ketoses; ribose, mannose, xylose and glucose gave no activity; D-ribulose and D-arabinose were not tested; the D-arabitol product is named D-xylulose from an NADH assay only.
Wong et al. 1993 abstract: C. albicans ArDH catalyzes D-arabitol + NAD <--> D-ribulose + NADH.

reviewer: Read-only review r2190_identity_review_20261019 (Claude Code session, 2026-10-19); verdict: product wrong, inferred (strong); regiochemistry open.
limits: The D-ribulose (C-2) versus D-xylulose (C-4) regiochemistry is not resolved by Y. lipolytica data.
The new species has no other reaction, so R2190 carries no steady-state flux after this change.
EC 1.1.1.250 on this gene is homology-level; the GPR is not experimental validation of this reaction.
Bounds are kept; the direction of R2190 was not reviewed.
